thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: INCIDENT P1 — Detecting p99 streaming latency spike and stalls across EU region. Multiple SSE/WebSocket sessions reporting stalled chunks and proxy timeouts. Paging on-call now. :rotating_light:

alex.m: oncall acked, joining. pulling p95/p99 dashboards now.

sara.li: saw a big jump ~22:04 UTC, p95 from 150ms -> 1.2s, p99 to 5.8s. Several customer sessions dropped mid-stream.

rafael: confirming, proxy (edge-eu-1) shows repeated 502s and upstream write timeouts. Possible slow consumers causing backpressure.

maya_ops: posting quick logs from the proxy cluster:```
[edge-eu-1] 2026-03-17T22:04:21Z upstream write timeout to backends (code=ETIMEDOUT)
[edge-eu-1] 2026-03-17T22:04:22Z client slowread, window=0
[edge-eu-1] 2026-03-17T22:04:23Z keepalive dropped, conn-id=19724
```

lina_support: customer-impact: 3 customers (two enterprise) reported truncated streamed responses and repeated reconnects. CS triage opened.

eng-runtime: initial hypothesis: client-side backpressure combined with proxy buffer exhaustion -> long stall then timeout. Also seeing a small spike in KV cache hits leading to synchronous disk fallback on one replica.

alex.m: running quick probe to confirm if it's origin or proxy. curl against SSE endpoint from inside EU coloc:```
curl -N https://edge-eu-1.redwood.ai/stream?model=redwood-large
# initial tokens stream, then silence ~8s, socket stays open
```

sara.li: can we flip traffic to secondary region for affected customers? Are there routing policies for live failover?

eng-runtime: we have region fallback but sticky sessions mean some clients will keep trying EU. Recommend two actions: 1) throttle long-poll SSE clients aggressively at edge (drop idle readers after 10s zero-write), 2) enable proxy write buffering fallback to avoid synchronous stalls.

maya_ops: applying temporary proxy config on edge-eu-1 now: `proxy_write_timeout 10s; proxy_buffer_size 8k; proxy_busy_buffers_size 16k;` will roll in canary to 3 nodes.

incident-bot: ACTION: maya_ops is applying config canary to edge-eu-1 nodes (3/12). Monitoring for p99 improvement.

rafael: also enabling connection heartbeat from server-side for SSE (send padding every 3s) to keep client buffers warm. Pushing canary to runtime instances now.

lina_support: informing impacted customers: quick note sent that team is investigating and mitigation is being rolled. CS will update if we need to initiate incident bridge.

alex.m: after canary: p95 -> 200ms, p99 dropped from 5.8s -> 900ms on canary nodes, no more truncated streams seen on those nodes. Canary looks promising.

eng-runtime: still seeing a couple of replicas with high disk I/O on KV cache fallback; marking them as non-primary for routing to avoid tail latency. Starting controlled eviction.

oncall-l3: taking over for remediation. I'll continue with node eviction and proxy param rollout across EU. Tagging @sara.li for follow-up on postmortem.

sara.li: ack, I'll track SLO impacts and open an incident postmortem ticket. Need logs for p95/p99 and affected customer list.

maya_ops: full rollout complete across edge-eu-1. Observed p99 steady at ~700-900ms, error rate back to baseline. Keeping increased heartbeat enabled for 2 hours.

lina_support: CS updated customers: mitigations applied, monitoring. No escalations at this time.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated. Root cause candidate: client slow-read + proxy buffer exhaustion + KV cache fallback on a subset of replicas. Postmortem assigned to eng-runtime and ops.

eng-runtime: next steps: add passive backpressure detection in edge layer, tune buffer sizes per connection class, instrument KV fallback path to surface synchronous I/O.

alex.m: handoff to daytime oncall in 3h. I'll leave notes in the incident ticket with timeline and commands used. :thumbsup:

oncall-l3: Handoff accepted. I'll keep watch for 4h and then update incident as resolved if no regressions. Closing on-call page for now. :white_check_mark:
